memory_update.text: TLN should remain a reference anchor for direct nuclear-to-hyperscaler power procurement, but it is not the main underfollowed discovery target because attention has risen after Amazon/AWS agreements.

POWL deserves follow-up as a relatively pure electrical-distribution equipment beneficiary after disclosing a >$400M data-center order, despite having moved out of the ideal small/mid-cap hunting range.

MYRG is a second-order underfollowed grid/interconnection execution candidate; survival to Layer 2 depends on finding explicit backlog or margin evidence tied to data centers, substations, transmission, or utility interconnection work.

ASPI is a speculative HALEU/fuel-cycle shadow candidate; it should be carried only with strict falsification checks around regulatory approval, technical validation, binding offtake, and capital availability.

Need a focused Layer 2 search on regional utilities and municipal/public-power entities with high data-center interconnection queues, because many direct beneficiaries may be regulated utilities whose AI exposure is buried in rate-base filings rather than investor presentations.

node: Power generation, grid interconnection, transmission services, nuclear fuel/enrichment, reactor components, and AI data-center power procurement
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the AI power/grid/nuclear-fuel node found one reference anchor with direct hyperscaler nuclear-data-center monetization and three underfollowed or speculative discovery names tied to electrical distribution equipment, transmission/data-center electrical construction, and potential HALEU/nuclear-fuel supply. The strongest direct evidence is Talen's Amazon/AWS nuclear PPA relationship and Powell's disclosed >$400M data-center order. MYR Group is a second-order grid/interconnection and electrical-construction beneficiary. ASP Isotopes is a speculative shadow candidate because HALEU/fuel-cycle relevance is plausible but commercial readiness and regulatory execution require heavy verification.
